mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during Fed rate hikes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weaker labor market conditions reduce risk aversion and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 4% in the current month.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (household spending) above 1,200 imply pent-up demand that translates into a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return when the two-month HOUST > 1,200 pattern occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 5% relative to the prior month precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing signals economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO falls by >5% in the month prior.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both rise simultaneously over a 3-month window, the interaction creates a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return by reinforcing easing and labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE each increase over the past 3 months
regime_hint: Dual easing: monetary and labor market loosening
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not positive when the joint rise in both proxies is not detected (e.g., one moves up, the other flat).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 10,000 for three consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to rising labor market stress.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the three-month decline in PAYEMS occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time spike in GDPC1 (GDP) above trend by 2% in the quarter prior to prediction is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds trend by >2% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return when GDPC1 shows the specified quarterly over-trend.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 8% in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 60 days due to weak consumer demand signals.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >8% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when RSAFS declines by >8% over two months.
